sentences.text:
Counsel for Respondent :- C.S.C.,Nipun Singh
Hon'ble Ashwani Kumar Mishra,J.
Hon'ble Anish Kumar Gupta,J.
1.

Fifteen petitioners have joined in the present petition instituted with the prayer to command the District Magistrate/Special Land Acquisition Officer, Moradabad to pay compensation in respect of plot no.788 (area 1.311 hect), 805 (area 1.048 hectare), 781 (area 1.445 hectare) and 8.10 (area 1.441 hectare) situated at village Shahpur Tigari, Tehsil and district Moradabad, directly to the petitioners in proportion of their share.
As per the petitioners they have acquired right over the plot pursuant to sale deed executed in their favor by Mayank Sahkari Awas Samiti Ltd., Moradabad.

It is asserted that the land was subsequently acquired by the housing board pursuant to a notification issued Avinash Chandra Sharma And 14 Others vs State Of Up And 4 Others on 12 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169618424/
1 under Section 28 and 32 of the U.P. Awas Evam Vikas Parishad Adhinium, 1965 which corresponds to Section 4 and 6 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: An award was also declared pursuant to the acquisition of land in the year 2010.

Petitioners submit that though they have perfected right in respect of different parcels of the acquired land, yet their claims for payment of compensation are not been bestowed any consideration by the board.

2. Sri Nipun Singh, appearing for the housing board has opposed the claim of petitioners on the ground that specific share or the parcel of land over which the petitioners are claiming right has not been specified in the writ, and since their entitlement is not established, no direction to be issued to the State authorities for consideration of petitioners' claim for payment of compensation.
Learned State counsel has also taken a similar stand.
3. We have heard learned counsel for the parties and have perused the materials on record.

4. Though petitioners state that they have a share in the land originally owned by the fifth respondent-Society, pursuant to sale-deeds allegedly executed in their favor, but the alleged sale deed is not on record.
No material exists to show that such a sale deed was executed in their favor or their right stood crystallized over any specified portion of the acquired land.

No writ of mandamus,
in such circumstances, can be issued in favor of the petitioners, as is prayed.

5. However, in the facts and circumstances of the present case, we are of the opinion that the petitioners be permitted to approach fourth respondent alongwith all materials in support of their claim of ownership over part of the acquired land.
The certified copy of the sale deed etc. shall be specifically presented before the Special Land Acquisition Officer.

The Special Land Acquisition Officer shall examined the claim of the petitioners and in the event there is no dispute with regard to their entitlement necessary action would be taken after notice to fifth respondent and the housing board for release of compensation to the rightful owner.

However, if there is any dispute relating to entitlement before the Collector concerned, he shall take note of the provisions contained under Section 30 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 or any other applicable provision which may be attracted in the facts of the present case and proceed, as per law.
The required action in that regard would be taken within a period of four months from the date of presentation of certified copy of this order.
6. The writ petition is, consequently, disposed of.

Order Date :- 12.4.2024 RA  Avinash Chandra Sharma And 14 Others vs State Of Up And 4 Others on 12 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169618424/
